lens: PartForge: geometry, export, drawings and printables
title: Hole Stack
tagline: Clearance, counterbore, countersink, tapped hole and nut pocket for an M-size, worked from fasteners_metric.json with each number's confidence carried into the OpenSCAD and the FLIGHT rows.
pitch: PartForge's fastener table is handed to the designer model as text and the doctrine tells it which column to use for what; the first dry run showed what happens when a model does that arithmetic itself. Hole Stack is a fifth selector: give it a size (M2-M20), a head style (socket, countersunk, button, none), whether a washer sits under the head, the clearance series (fine/medium/coarse) and the plate thickness, and it returns the finished hole stack as numbers, as an OpenSCAD module with $fn=fn_tol(d) on every cylinder and a comment on every dimension naming its table field, standard and confidence, as FLIGHT holes/bores rows whose provenance follows the row's confidence (ISO 273 clearance is likely with a named standard, so tol_src source with the table field as tol_ref; cbore_d_mm is recall on all 12 rows, so the counterbore is sized from the table's own documented alternative, knurled head dk + 0.4 mm, and the recall tool size is shown beside it as [recall]), with the H12/H13/H14 band of the clearance hole taken from fits.json's IT widths for the size step, and as a dimensioned SVG cross-section. A size or field the table does not hold is refused by name.
whyNow: /home/user/Partforge/data/tables/fasteners_metric.json columns: cbore_d_mm is RECALL ('any value >= shcs_head_d_knurled_mm + 0.4 works'), shcs_head_d_mm carries the WARNING 'size counterbores from shcs_head_d_knurled_mm or cbore_d_mm, never from this column', csk/button fields null at small sizes; /home/user/Partforge/docs/data/PROVENANCE.md section 1 'Doctrine' prescribes exactly this stack (tap at minor_D1_mm, drill tap_drill_mm, clearance_medium_mm by default, counterbore cbore_d_mm or knurled dk + 0.4 and cbore_depth_flush_mm, hex pockets to nut_ac_min_mm and nut_h_mm/locknut_h_mm). /home/user/Partforge/README.md Flight grade lists four worked selectors (dbPickORing, dbPickDrill, dbPickStock, dbBoreMm at index.html:5041-5137) and none for holes; /home/user/Partforge/docs/roadmap-evaluation.md line 42 records the doctrine's hand-typed UN clearances being one fit class off the app's own fasteners_un.json, which is the failure a table-reading generator removes.
computes: Inputs: size key, head style, washer flag, clearance series, plate_t, locknut flag. Logic: row lookup; clearance d from clearance_{fine,medium,coarse}_mm; band from fits.json: find the step with from_mm < d <= to_mm and take it_um['12'|'13'|'14'] (6-10 mm step: 150/220/360 um) giving +IT/0 for an H hole; counterbore primary = shcs_head_d_knurled_mm + 0.4, depth = cbore_depth_flush_mm (+ washer_t_mm if washer), tool size cbore_d_mm shown as recall; countersink from csk_head_d_mm at 90 deg and csk_head_h_mm (recall, refused if null); tapped hole modelled at minor_D1_mm with tap_drill_mm and the stainless alternative; nut pocket across-corners >= nut_ac_sharp_mm (certain) with nut_ac_min_mm beside it, depth nut_h_mm or locknut_h_mm; engagement note from min_engagement_6061T6_8_8_mm. Outputs: JSON, OpenSCAD module text, FLIGHT rows, SVG section with callouts.
dataNeeded: Snapshot whole with tools/snapshot.mjs: data/tables/fasteners_metric.json (58,241 B, 12 rows with field_confidence) and data/tables/fits.json (17,453 B, 13 size steps with it_um and shaft deviations). Provenance excerpt of DECL-BEGIN..DECL-END (16,204 B) so the emitted FLIGHT rows can be validated by the app's parseFlight and flightLint in the test. Optionally fasteners_un.json (108,390 B) for the inch twin; the budget allows it but the first build should stay metric. About 95-200 KB.
existingOverlap: PartForge's dbHints() quotes table rows to the designer and the doctrine prescribes the stack in prose; the four selectors cover O-rings, drills, stock and bores. The counterbore and clearance numbers exist as data; no code turns them into geometry, FLIGHT rows or a drawing. This differs by being the worked selector the README's own argument ('the lookups are worked, not quoted') calls for, applied to holes.
honestyRisks: The main way to lie here is to stamp a recall field as cited. Provenance is derived mechanically from field_confidence: only certain/likely fields with a named standard become tol_src source; recall fields become default with the field name and '[recall]' in the note, and the test asserts no emitted source row traces to a recall field. The +0.4 mm counterbore rule is the table's own note, quoted, not invented; the IT-grade band is labelled likely as fits.json labels it. Null fields refuse by name (M2 countersink). The OpenSCAD cannot be compiled here, so the test checks it structurally and the README says the compile gate has not been passed.
testPlan: node --test and python3 -m unittest: (1) M6 socket, medium, no washer: clearance 6.6 with band +0.220/0 (fits.json step 6-10, IT13 220 um), counterbore 10.62 (10.22 + 0.4) depth 6.5, tool size 11.0 shown as recall; with washer depth 8.1; tapped at D1 4.917, drill 5.0, stainless 5.2; nut pocket across-corners 11.547 sharp / 11.05 min, depth 5.2, locknut 6.0 recall. (2) M3 countersink 6.72 at 90 deg; M2 countersink refused naming csk_head_d_mm null. (3) M7 refused listing the 12 keys. (4) Every number in the emitted module text equals a row field value or a documented sum of them (regex all numbers, match against the row and the two rules). (5) parseFlight on the emitted rows: dropped 0, demoted 0; flightLint on the module text: []. (6) No emitted row with tol_src source references a field whose field_confidence is recall (assert over all 12 sizes x 4 head styles). (7) Page smoke at 390 px.
landing: PartForge index.html DB block: dbHoleStack() as the fifth selector, surfaced in dbHints() for requests that name a thread, and in ⚙ Settings → Look up real hardware; headless `lookup` would return it. To ship: pass tests/flight-db.test.mjs-style assertions, flow through tools/db/embed.mjs so the browser copy is the table projection, and add the inch twin from fasteners_un.json with its related_hardware recall rules.
notes: Verified fasteners_metric field_confidence marks cbore_d_mm/csk/button as recall and the cbore column text 'knurled + 0.4'; PROVENANCE §1 doctrine prescribes this stack. Mechanical provenance from field_confidence is the strong part.

Verified M6 row (clearance 6.6, knurled dk 10.22, cbore 11.0 recall, depth 6.5, D1 4.917, drill 5.0) and the cbore_d_mm RECALL warning; provenance derived mechanically from field_confidence is exactly the discipline the roadmap asks for.

Every M6 number in the test plan matches the fasteners_metric row exactly (clearance 6.6, knurled 10.22, cbore 11.0/6.5, D1 4.917, drill 5.0/5.2, nut AC 11.547/11.05, nut_h 5.2, locknut 6.0) and the cbore_d_mm recall warning is in columns. Provenance derived mechanically from field_confidence is the right design.
